source.title: Learning Faster without Deeper Networks: A*-Inspired Batch Selection for Efficient CNN Training
source.authors: Anxhelo Shehu; Enes Stastoli; Arben Çela

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Applies a batch-ordering strategy to low-resolution medical image classification and reports test-set outcomes in that setting.
record.gate_note: The paper tests A*-BS against random batch shuffling on the same lightweight CNN. It does not test the listed claim versions. ResNet benchmark values are reported from cited work, not generated by this study, so they are excluded. Wall-clock timings measure training cost, not generalization, and are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study varies batch ordering and measures test ACC and AUC. It does not vary batch size, optimizer, width, dropout, or convolutional versus fully connected architecture, and does not measure random-label fitting, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorization-based removal. Its citation of large-batch generalization work does not constitute a test of V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that A*-BS improves ACC and AUC over random shuffling on all twelve evaluated tasks, with dataset-dependent gains, and complements lightweight CNNs without closing every gap to published ResNet benchmarks. These conclusions rest on single-run ablations; the ResNet accuracy comparison is not a controlled head-to-head experiment.
record.recipe_differences: Changes the within-epoch batch order using loss and reuse counts; it does not test the original claim's interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the reported test ACC and AUC; only one training run per dataset-strategy pair is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: With architecture, optimizer, learning rate, batch size and epoch count held fixed, A*-BS yields higher test ACC and AUC than random shuffling on all twelve tasks. Results use the best validation-ACC checkpoint from one run per condition; uncertainty and statistical significance are not established.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing batch ordering to A*-BS can improve held-out ACC and AUC for a lightweight CNN on the evaluated MedMNIST 2D tasks.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Control, Decision and Information Technologies
record.problems: The controlled ablation reports a single training run per dataset-strategy pair and no paired statistical test or multi-seed uncertainty. The ResNet comparison uses published benchmark values and is not a controlled head-to-head experiment.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results omitted. The paper's ResNet comparisons and wall-clock measurements are not rows: ResNet figures are cited prior-work results, and timing does not measure generalization.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All 48 values and paired baselines match Table II. Their states remain cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because none measures a listed version's effect. The batch-ordering improvement itself is directly measured. Published ResNet accuracy values and training-time results are correctly excluded from claim-linked rows.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization under different tuning regimes.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
